Injury Burden Intensity.description: overall physical burden of the injuries: 0 minimal, 4 catastrophic/multiple major injuries

Treatment Burden.description: extent of treatment, surgery and ongoing care: 0 none or minimal, 3 extensive surgery and long-term care

Work Impact Severity.description: loss of working capacity: 0 none, 3 total incapacity

Legal Procedural Complexity.description: procedural complexity of the proceeding: 0 straightforward, 3 heavily contested

Psychological Injury Emphasis.description: weight the decision gives to psychological injury: 0 none, 2 central

Liability Clarity.description: how clear fault is: 0 seriously disputed, 2 clear or admitted

Causation Complexity.description: difficulty attributing the condition to the accident: 0 straightforward, 2 heavily contested

Pre-existing Condition Salience.description: how prominent a prior condition is in the decision: 0 absent, 2 central

rubric_source: recovered from the original codings by stage 12
limitation: The original coding rubric is not recorded in this repository. These scale descriptions were reconstructed from column names and observed ranges, so disagreement mixes unreliability with rubric drift. The second reader is also a language model: independent in context and prompt, not in kind.
system_prompt:
You are coding NSW motor accident decisions for a research dataset. Read the decision text supplied and assign each ordinal score from the text alone.

Score each dimension INDEPENDENTLY. A decision describing a severe case will score high on some dimensions and not others: severe physical injury does not by itself imply a contested proceeding, a disputed liability, or a prominent psychological component. Judge each scale against its own definition and resist letting an overall impression of severity carry across the scales.

If the text does not support a judgement on a dimension, give the lowest score rather than guessing upward, and say so in `uncertain`.
